qa.a: Not measurably: 38 of 59 identical prices (64%) were flat from 14 to 21 Nov, the median change was 0%, and the same-item basket rose 2.7% without one Takealot outlier.

qa.a: For identical brands Superb Hyper (92.5 vs Pick n Pay, ±5.9, 17 items) and Makro (cheapest on 18 of 31 items). For thrifty shoppers buying own brands, Pick n Pay (cheapest-equivalent index 90.8, 101 items).
No clear premium: Checkers Sixty60 indexes 101.7 (±5.3, n=39) against the item median, and the quick-commerce channel 101.6 (±5.2).
qa.q: Is quick commerce charging a premium?

qa.a: Tins & spreads (9.0% own-brand saving) and staples (8.7%); unit-price gaps reach 40–44% on rice, maize meal and dish liquid.
qa.q: Where are our name brands most exposed to own brands?

exec.catch: Collection started on 14 Nov 2026, so this rests on three daily-basket days and one Essentials day: within-month change covers 7 days and there is no October comparison. Online advertised prices, not till prices; retailers list different items.
exec.title: Prices held flat in November's first collection week; the money is in own brands, retailer choice and Black Friday timing
exec.so_what: With shelf prices steady and Black Friday demand building, the battle for the next four weeks is visibility and own-brand trade-down, not list-price moves: secure promo slots at the retailers that win head-to-head (Superb Hyper, Makro, Amazon) and defend staples and tins, where the own-brand saving is widest (9%).
exec.takeaway: 64% of identical item-retailer prices did not move between 14 and 21 Nov and the same-item basket rose only 2.7% without one Takealot nappy listing; Pick n Pay's own brands cut the Essentials basket by 16.9%, the median item spread is 43%, and Black Friday searches are 5x October's.

report.scope: Month to date, 1–30 Nov 2026 · price collection started 14 Nov 2026 (baseline) · 367 daily-basket prices on 14, 20, 21 Nov · Essentials Basket 21 Nov (317 prices, 11 retailers) · search trends Jun–15 Nov 2026

c1.sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT item, retailer, channel, price_zar p0 FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day='2026-11-14'), b AS (SELECT item, retailer, price_zar p1 FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day='2026-11-21'),
j AS (SELECT a.*, b.p1 FROM a JOIN b USING(item,retailer))
SELECT channel AS "Channel", COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(SUM(p0)::numeric,0) AS "14 Nov (R)", ROUND(SUM(p1)::numeric,0) AS "21 Nov (R)", ROUND((100*(SUM(p1)/SUM(p0)-1))::numeric,1) AS "Change %" FROM j GROUP BY channel ORDER BY 5
c1.title: Same-item basket change, 14 → 21 Nov, by channel
c1.subtitle: 59 identical item-retailer pairs seen on both days; sum of shelf prices

c2.sql: SELECT retailer AS "Retailer", items_same_brand AS "Items (same brand)", items_any_brand AS "Items (any brand)", ROUND(same_brand_index::numeric,1) AS "Same-brand index", ROUND(cheapest_equivalent_index::numeric,1) AS "Cheapest-equivalent index" FROM analyst.essentials_index WHERE day='2026-11-21' AND items_same_brand>=5 ORDER BY same_brand_index
c2.title: Essentials Index, 21 Nov 2026 (100 = median retailer)
c2.subtitle: 124-item basket; each retailer indexed over the items it priced (see item counts)

c3.sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT item, retailer, same_brand_price_zar AS pr FROM analyst.essentials_prices WHERE day='2026-11-21' AND same_brand_price_zar IS NOT NULL)
SELECT b.retailer AS "Retailer", COUNT(*) AS "Common items", ROUND(AVG(100*b.pr/a.pr)::numeric,1) AS "Index vs Pick n Pay (100)", ROUND((1.645*STDDEV(100*b.pr/a.pr)/SQRT(COUNT(*)))::numeric,1) AS "Margin (pts)"
FROM p a JOIN p b ON a.item=b.item AND a.retailer='Pick n Pay' AND b.retailer<>'Pick n Pay' GROUP BY b.retailer HAVING COUNT(*)>=9 ORDER BY 3
c3.title: Head-to-head vs Pick n Pay on identical items, 21 Nov
c3.subtitle: Same brand, same size, same day; below 100 = cheaper than Pick n Pay

c4.sql:
WITH m AS (SELECT day, item, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY price_zar) med FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day>='2026-11-01' AND day<'2026-12-01' GROUP BY day,item HAVING COUNT(*)>=2),
r AS (SELECT p.channel, p.retailer, 100*p.price_zar/m.med ratio FROM analyst.retail_prices p JOIN m USING(day,item))
SELECT retailer AS "Retailer", channel, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(ratio)::numeric,1) AS "Price index", ROUND((1.645*STDDEV(ratio)/SQRT(COUNT(*)))::numeric,1) AS "Margin (pts)" FROM r GROUP BY retailer, channel ORDER BY 4
c4.title: Daily-basket price index by retailer, 14–21 Nov
c4.subtitle: Retailer price ÷ item median that day × 100; items with 2+ retailers

c5.sql:
WITH m AS (SELECT day, item, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY price_zar) med, COUNT(*) k FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day>='2026-11-01' AND day<'2026-12-01' GROUP BY day,item HAVING COUNT(*)>=2),
r AS (SELECT p.channel, p.retailer, 100*p.price_zar/m.med ratio FROM analyst.retail_prices p JOIN m USING(day,item))
SELECT channel AS "Channel", COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(ratio)::numeric,1) AS "Price index (100 = item median)", ROUND((1.645*STDDEV(ratio)/SQRT(COUNT(*)))::numeric,1) AS "Margin (pts)" FROM r GROUP BY channel ORDER BY 3
c5.title: Price index by channel, 14–21 Nov
c5.subtitle: Margins ±3–5 pts: channel gaps are mostly within noise

c6.sql: SELECT category AS "Category", COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(same_brand_price_zar - cheapest_equivalent_zar)::numeric,2) AS "Avg saving (R)", ROUND(AVG(100*(same_brand_price_zar - cheapest_equivalent_zar)/same_brand_price_zar)::numeric,1) AS "Own-brand saving %", ROUND((1.645*STDDEV(100*(same_brand_price_zar - cheapest_equivalent_zar)/same_brand_price_zar)/SQRT(COUNT(*)))::numeric,1) AS margin_pts FROM analyst.essentials_prices WHERE day='2026-11-21' AND same_brand_price_zar IS NOT NULL AND cheapest_equivalent_zar IS NOT NULL GROUP BY category ORDER BY 4 DESC
c6.title: Own-brand saving by category, 21 Nov
c6.subtitle: Same-brand price minus cheapest equivalent, % of same-brand price; all retailers

c7.sql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM analyst.retail_unit_prices WHERE day>='2026-11-01' AND day<'2026-12-01'),
pairs(house, name_item, name_ret, label) AS (VALUES
 ('Checkers Housebrand rice 2kg','Tastic rice 2kg',NULL,'Rice 2kg: Checkers Housebrand vs Tastic'),
 ('Ritebrand maize meal 5kg','White Star maize meal 5kg','Shoprite','Maize meal 5kg: Ritebrand vs White Star (both Shoprite)'),
 ('Checkers Housebrand dishwashing liquid 750ml','Sunlight dishwashing liquid 750ml',NULL,'Dish liquid 750ml: Checkers Housebrand vs Sunlight'),
 ('Woolworths full cream milk 2L','Clover full cream milk 2L',NULL,'Milk 2L: Woolworths own vs Clover')),
x AS (SELECT label, (SELECT AVG(price_per_unit_zar) FROM u WHERE item=house) h, (SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY price_per_unit_zar) FROM u WHERE item=name_item AND (name_ret IS NULL OR retailer=name_ret)) nb, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM u WHERE item=name_item AND (name_ret IS NULL OR retailer=name_ret)) nn, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM u WHERE item=house) hn FROM pairs)
SELECT label AS "Pair", hn AS "House n", ROUND(h::numeric,2) AS "House brand (R per unit)", nn AS "Name n", ROUND(nb::numeric,2) AS "Name brand (R per unit)", ROUND((100*(h/nb-1))::numeric,0) AS "House-brand gap %" FROM x ORDER BY 6
rows: Dish liquid 750ml: Checkers Housebrand vs Sunlight
Maize meal 5kg: Ritebrand vs White Star (both Shoprite)
c7.title: House brand vs name brand, price per kg/litre, Nov
c7.subtitle: Negative = house brand cheaper per unit; 14–21 Nov

c9.sql: SELECT day AS "Day", item AS "Item", retailer AS "Retailer", previous_price_zar AS "Before (R)", price_zar AS "After (R)", ROUND(change_pct::numeric,0) AS "Change %" FROM analyst.retail_price_changes WHERE day>='2026-11-01' AND day<'2026-12-01' AND change_pct<=-10 AND NOT (item='Black Cat peanut butter 400g' AND retailer='Makro') AND NOT (item='Jungle Oats 1kg' AND retailer='Amazon.co.za') ORDER BY change_pct
c9.title: Likely promotions: price cuts of 10%+ vs previous sighting
c9.subtitle: 20–21 Nov; two reversals of listing errors excluded

c10.sql:
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month',day),'YYYY-MM') AS "Month", COUNT(*)/5 AS weeks,
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='shoprite specials')::numeric,1) AS "Shoprite specials",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='spar specials')::numeric,1) AS "SPAR specials",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='checkers specials')::numeric,1) AS "Checkers specials",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='pick n pay specials')::numeric,1) AS "Pick n Pay specials",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='woolworths specials')::numeric,1) AS "Woolworths specials"
FROM analyst.search_interest WHERE term_group='retail: specials by retailer · 12 months' AND day>='2026-06-01' AND day<'2026-12-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
c10.title: Searches for retailer specials, monthly average, Jun–Nov 2026
c10.subtitle: Relative interest 0–100 within group; Nov = 3 weeks to 15 Nov

c11.sql:
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month',day),'YYYY-MM') AS "Month",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='black friday')::numeric,1) AS "Black Friday",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='takealot')::numeric,1) AS "Takealot",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='shein')::numeric,1) AS "Shein",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='temu')::numeric,1) AS "Temu",
ROUND(AVG(interest) FILTER (WHERE term='amazon south africa')::numeric,1) AS "Amazon SA"
FROM analyst.search_interest WHERE term_group='marketplace: online shopping · 12 months' AND day>='2026-06-01' AND day<'2026-12-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
c11.title: Online shopping searches, monthly average, Jun–Nov 2026
c11.subtitle: Relative interest 0–100 within group; Nov = 3 weeks to 15 Nov

c12.sql: SELECT item AS "Item", COUNT(*) AS "Retailers", ROUND(MIN(price_zar)::numeric,2) AS "Cheapest (R)", ROUND(MAX(price_zar)::numeric,2) AS "Dearest (R)", ROUND((100*(MAX(price_zar)/MIN(price_zar)-1))::numeric,0) AS "Spread %" FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day='2026-11-21' GROUP BY item HAVING COUNT(*)>=3 ORDER BY 5 DESC LIMIT 15
c12.title: Top 15 price spreads, cheapest vs dearest retailer, 21 Nov
c12.subtitle: Of 22 items listed by 3+ retailers; the other 7 spread 3–36%

steps: Within-month change (section 1): analyst.retail_prices on 14 Nov 2026 (first collection day, baseline) vs 21 Nov 2026 (latest), only the 59 item-retailer pairs seen on both days.
Essentials Index (section 2): analyst.essentials_index and analyst.essentials_prices for 21 Nov 2026, the only Essentials day in the period; head-to-heads recomputed over items both retailers priced.
Retailer/channel index and spreads (sections 3, 5): analyst.retail_prices for 14, 20 and 21 Nov; moves from analyst.retail_price_changes for 20–21 Nov vs the previous sighting.
House-brand gap (section 4): analyst.retail_unit_prices 14–21 Nov (price per kg/litre); category own-brand saving from essentials_prices 21 Nov.

Demand look-back (section 6): analyst.search_interest groups 'retail: specials by retailer · 12 months' and 'marketplace: online shopping · 12 months', weekly values averaged by month, Jun 2026 to 15 Nov 2026; Nov–Dec 2025 used only as seasonal reference.
trust: Same item, same retailer, same day comparisons throughout; 90% margins given next to every index.
Counts of unchanged prices, promotions and rises are full counts of what was collected.
Search trends rest on 4–5 weekly values per month in consistent term groups.
limits: Price collection started 14 Nov 2026: no figures exist for earlier months, and 'within-month' means 7 days.
Retailers list different items online, so indices for retailers with under ~15 items are indicative only.
Search interest is relative within its group and November is partial (to 15 Nov).

- Staples show an 8.7% own-brand saving (±3.6, n=46), over double personal care at 3.7% (n=47).
- A promo can beat the house brand: Iwisa 5kg at R9.00/kg on Amazon undercut Ritebrand's R9.60/kg.
- Household's own-brand saving is 5.1% (±2.8, n=48) despite a 44% unit gap on dish liquid.
sections.note: House-brand unit prices rest on only 8 rows (2 per product): treat the four pairs as indicative examples. Category savings come from the Essentials Basket on 21 Nov, mostly Pick n Pay shelves.

sections.question: Where are the widest price spreads, and who ran promotions or raised prices?
sections.takeaway: On 21 Nov the 22 items at 3+ retailers had a median 43% cheapest-to-dearest gap (10 above 50%); on 20–21 Nov we saw 10 likely promotions averaging 24% off against 12 rises of 10% or more.

explainers.why: At a 43% median, a shopper who checks two stores saves a lot, and the brand's price image is hard to control.

risks: Only 7 days of price history since collection started on 14 Nov: no month-on-month or seasonal price baseline yet.
Retailers price different items (9–79 in the Essentials Index), so small-sample indices (Takealot, Clicks, Amazon head-to-head) are indicative.
Online advertised prices can differ from till and loyalty prices; listing errors (two found) can create false promotions.
Own-brand saving is observable mainly at Pick n Pay and Shoprite; other retailers' own-brand pull is understated.
November search values stop at 15 Nov, before Black Friday week.
actions: Lock Black Friday and payday (25 Nov–1 Dec) promo funding at the head-to-head price winners: Superb Hyper, Makro and Amazon.co.za.
Defend staples and tins against own brands with multi-buy or pack-price promotions; the own-brand saving there is about 9%.
Raise Dis-Chem's household increases (Sunlight, Omo, Domestos +25–28%) and Takealot's outliers in account reviews this week.
Set a per-retailer price corridor (e.g. ±10% of item median) and flag breaches, since one channel spans 26 index points.
Re-run this pack at month-end with the full November to measure Black Friday promo depth and post-promo price returns.
Plan December on last year's post-Black Friday search drop (42.3 in Nov 2025 to 1.0 in Dec 2025).
findings: Shelf prices were stable: 64% of 59 identical prices unchanged 14→21 Nov; basket +2.7% ex one outlier.
Pick n Pay's own brands save shoppers 16.9% (±3.0, 79 items); its cheapest-equivalent index is 90.8.
Superb Hyper is 7.5% cheaper than Pick n Pay on identical items; Checkers is dearest of the big grocers at 107.1.
Retailer matters more than channel: Amazon 90.9 vs Takealot 117.2, while channels overlap within 98–105.
Median spread of 43% across 22 items; 12 price rises of 10%+ outnumbered 10 likely promotions.
Black Friday searches are 5x October's level and SPAR specials are 42% up on October.
